name: Heinz-Georg Baus
profile: Founder of German DIY/home-improvement chain Bauhaus (founded 1960 in Mannheim). Died May 2016, aged 82.
interesting_fact: Died in May 2016 aged 82; Bauhaus was Germany's first DIY store chain, opened in Mannheim in 1960 on the American model.
notes: Deceased (May 2016) per DIY International and Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz-Georg_Baus). Not a candidate.

name: Reimann family
current_role: Family owners of JAB Holding Company (Luxembourg-based investment vehicle; stakes in Keurig Dr Pepper, Coty, Peet's, Krispy Kreme, Panera etc.)
profile: German family descended from chemist Ludwig Reimann, who joined Johann Adam Benckiser's chemicals firm in the 1820s and married into the founding family. Albert Reimann Jr. expanded into consumer goods; the business became Reckitt Benckiser, and four of his adopted children own most of JAB, run by professional partners.
interesting_fact: JAB takes its name from the initials of Johann Adam Benckiser, the founder of the 19th-century chemicals firm the family inherited.
notes: Family entry listed only on Forbes 1996-2000, so it's unclear which members are meant. Very private family; JAB says it is run by professional partners. Best route is JAB's corporate contact form. Avoid the Nazi-era history unless relevant.

name: Eric Duval
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Groupe Duval (Paris-area family real estate group; CEO is his daughter Pauline Boucon Duval)
profile: French entrepreneur who founded Groupe Duval in 1994 as a real estate developer. It grew into a family group of about 6,000 staff in 20 countries and roughly €1bn in revenue, spanning development, retail parks, Odalys tourist residences and golf. His children now run day-to-day operations, and the group is expanding in Africa and into energy-transition services.
interesting_fact: Groupe Duval bought Odalys in 2000, UGolf in 2009 and Bluegreen in 2022, which made it Europe's leading golf operator and the world's 5th largest.
deep_cut_fact: The group marked its 30th anniversary on 19 September 2024 at the Palais Brongniart (the old Paris stock exchange). Its plans include renewable energy and energy-transition services.
notes: Florian Silnicki is listed as Directeur de la Communication and Philippine Barneville as Responsable de la communication. The group's renewable-energy activities fit the podcast angle. Low personal media profile.

name: Brian Acton
current_role: Executive Chairman, Signal Technology Foundation (co-founded 2018); also listed as interim CEO of Signal Messenger LLC
profile: Stanford computer scientist and early Yahoo engineer who co-founded WhatsApp with Jan Koum in 2009. Facebook bought it in 2014 for about $19-22bn. He left in 2017, put $50m into creating the Signal Foundation, and with his wife Tegan runs Wildcard Giving, Sunlight Giving and related charities holding over $1bn.
interesting_fact: In 2009 both Twitter (May) and Facebook (August) turned him down for jobs. Five years later Facebook bought WhatsApp for about $19bn. He had tweeted that Twitter's rejection was 'ok' because it would have been a long commute.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yahoo, he grew up in Michigan and Central Florida (Lake Howell High School). In 1992 he worked as a systems administrator at Rockwell International, then did product testing at Apple and Adobe. He joined Yahoo in 1996.
notes: His $50m to Signal was structured as an interest-free loan. I found no published press email for Signal (privacy@signal.org is for data requests only). He's privacy-minded and rarely gives interviews, so the best route is probably via the Signal Foundation or his X account.

name: Jack Cockwell
current_role: Former President & CEO of Brookfield (1991-2002); shareholder of Partners Ltd, which holds Brookfield's controlling voting shares
profile: South African-born accountant (born East London, 1941) who joined Touche Ross in Cape Town and was sent to Montreal in 1966. He joined the Bronfmans' Edper in 1968 and built it into the Brookfield empire, handing over to Bruce Flatt in 2002. His wealth comes largely from Brookfield shares held through the Partners partnership. He is a Member of the Order of Canada.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he gave $5m to Ryerson (now Toronto Metropolitan University) nursing school, renamed the Daphne Cockwell School of Nursing after his mother. In 2011 he gave $10m toward George Brown College's Limberlost Place, a 10-storey mass-timber building.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-1980s he bought land near Huntsville, Ontario, and created the Limberlost Forest and Wildlife Reserve, now over 10,000 acres and open to the public. As a teenager he represented his Scout troop at the 9th World Scout Jamboree in England (1957).
notes: In his 80s and keeps a low profile. The Brookfield press email is a corporate route, and the Limberlost email is for the reserve he founded (it's a general inquiry address). I couldn't confirm whether he is still on any Brookfield board in 2026.

name: Tung Chee Hwa
profile: Shipping heir (Orient Overseas/OOCL) and Hong Kong's first Chief Executive (1997-2005). He died on 8 September 2026, aged 89.
interesting_fact: He was Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader. In 2018 he and his brother sold the family's 68.7% stake in Orient Overseas to COSCO for about $4.3bn.
notes: Died 8 September 2026 (SCMP, AP, The Standard: https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/342223/Hong-Kongs-first-chief-executive-Tung-Chee-hwa-dies-at-89). Not a candidate.

name: Augusto Perfetti
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Giorgio) of Perfetti Van Melle, the Italian-Dutch confectionery group headquartered in Lainate (Italy) and Breda (Netherlands)
profile: Son of Ambrogio Perfetti, who started a chewing-gum business near Milan with brother Egidio in 1946. Augusto and Giorgio grew it, notably through the 2001 Van Melle merger, into Perfetti Van Melle: Mentos, Chupa Chups, Airheads, Brooklyn and Mondelez's former gum brands (Trident, Dentyne). Revenue is over $4.8bn. Professional managers run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He named his yacht and private jet after Mentos and Airheads, the company's best-selling brands. His father and uncle were inspired to start the business after seeing American WWII soldiers bring gum to Europe.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026, for the company's 80th anniversary, Lainate named a square near the plant 'Largo Ambrogio ed Egidio Perfetti'. A giant replica of the first Brooklyn gum pack ('la gomma del ponte', launched 1956) was unveiled there.
notes: He keeps a very low public profile and I found no interviews. The company route goes through Perfetti Van Melle corporate communications (no press email is published; the contact page lists a data-protection address only). Corrado Bianchi is CEO of PVM Italia.

name: Zhou Guodi
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with Cao Longxiang) as a principal owner of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical (济川药业, SSE: 600566), Taixing, Jiangsu
profile: Hurun lists Zhou Guodi together with Cao Longxiang as owners of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical. Jumpcan is a Jiangsu drugmaker with 4,000+ staff, focused on respiratory, paediatric, digestive and women's health, including the Pudilan brand. It went from state-owned to private in 1998 and listed in Shanghai via a 2013 reverse listing. I couldn't independently verify her personal role.
interesting_fact: Jumpcan went from state-owned to private shareholding in 1998 and first entered China's top-100 pharmaceutical manufacturers in 2001. It has since struck licensing deals for innovative drugs (e.g. with I-Mab in 2021 and Akeso in 2025).
notes: My web search quota ran out at this point, so verification is limited to the company site. Neither the company site nor any source I could reach names her. Cao Longxiang is the better-known figure (understood to be her husband/co-owner, not verified here). jc@jumpcan.com is the general/customer-service address.

name: Don Levin
current_role: Owner of D.R.L. Enterprises / Republic Brands (rolling papers: OCB, JOB, E-Z Wider) and owner of the AHL's Chicago Wolves
profile: Chicago entrepreneur, son of a used-car salesman. He bought a head shop called Adams Apple, saw demand for rolling papers, and started a distribution business that became Republic Brands. In 2000 he bought OCB and JOB from Vincent Bolloré. His group now owns a paper mill and a rolling-paper factory, with about $600m in estimated annual revenue.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Chicago Wolves hockey club on 24 January 1994 with Buddy Meyers and Grant Mulvey. The team has won two IHL Turner Cups (1998, 2000) and three AHL Calder Cups (2002, 2008, 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to follow his father into selling cars, until a friend talked him into buying a Chicago head shop named Adams Apple. Most customers came in for rolling papers, which led to his distribution business.
notes: Very low media profile apart from the Chicago Wolves. The Wolves' front office is probably the most approachable route; I couldn't read their site, so check chicagowolves.com for media relations. Republic's only published email is salesinfo@ (sales), so I didn't include it.

name: Caroline Hagen Kjos
current_role: Chair of the Board, Canica AS (Norway); Board member, Canica Switzerland
profile: Swiss-resident daughter of Norwegian Rimi founder Stein Erik Hagen. She became chair and majority owner of the family investment company Canica in 2014. Canica, based in Oslo and Pfäffikon SZ, has long been the largest shareholder in Orkla ASA and invests in industry, finance and real estate (including hardware chain Jernia).
interesting_fact: She holds a bachelor's in business administration from Parsons School of Design in New York.
deep_cut_fact: Canica traces back to Odd Hagen AS, a grocery business her grandfather started in Oslo in 1953. Her father opened the first three Rimi stores in 1977 with the slogan 'Easiest is Cheapest'.
notes: Sensitive timing: her father Stein Erik Hagen (Canica founder, Orkla chair 2006-2026) died on 4 May 2026, per Canica's site. Very private. The best route is Canica's Swiss office (post@canica.ch) or Oslo office. Canica Switzerland's CEO is Christer Kjos and Canica Norway's CEO is Jan Ole Stangeland.

name: Manuel Puig Rocha
current_role: Vice Chairman, Puig Brands (Barcelona; listed 2024), and its largest individual shareholder
profile: Grandson of Antonio Puig, who founded the Barcelona perfume and beauty house in 1914. He has been vice president of Puig since 2007, overseeing international subsidiaries. Puig owns Carolina Herrera, Paco Rabanne, Jean Paul Gaultier, Nina Ricci, Charlotte Tilbury and Byredo. It listed on the Spanish stock exchange in May 2024 at about €14bn; the family keeps the large majority of voting rights.
interesting_fact: The company's big break was the Milady lipstick in 1922, eight years after founding. Today at least 14 family members control Puig.
notes: Very low public profile. Marc Puig (his cousin) is chairman/CEO and the public face. Puig's website blocked automated access, so I couldn't capture the press/IR emails; check puig.com's press and investor pages manually. Search quota was exhausted while I was researching him.

name: Wang Chenghai
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with Luo Hongxia) as the owner behind 'Dingtong' (electronic components)
profile: Hurun China lists Wang Chenghai and Luo Hongxia as the wealth holders behind Dingtong, an electronic-components company (Hurun China 2021-2026, Hurun Global 2026). I couldn't verify further details because my web search quota ran out.
notes: Not verified because the search quota was exhausted. Unconfirmed lead to check: this is probably Dongguan Dingtong Precision Technology (东莞鼎通精密科技, STAR Market 688668), which makes connector components for communications/high-speed links. If so, it could be relevant to the data-center angle. Re-run research with search available.

name: Xu Ruotong
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with Xu Xudong) as an owner of XuSheng Auto Technology
profile: Hurun Global (2018-2026) and Hurun China (2017-2025) list Xu Ruotong together with Xu Xudong as wealth holders of XuSheng Auto Technology, an auto-components maker. I couldn't verify further details because my web search quota ran out.
notes: Not verified because the search quota was exhausted. Unconfirmed lead: probably Ningbo Xusheng Group (宁波旭升集团, SSE 603305), an aluminium die-casting supplier for EVs (including Tesla), chaired by Xu Xudong. Xu Ruotong's personal role is unknown. Re-run research.

name: Haluk Bayraktar
current_role: CEO, Baykar (Turkish UAV maker); TÜBİTAK board member; founder of the Türkiye Technology Team (T3) Foundation
profile: Istanbul-born (1978) industrial engineer who joined his father Özdemir's company Baykar after graduate study in the US. He worked on Turkey's first national UAV systems. As CEO he co-owns about 47.5% with brother Selçuk, and has turned Baykar into a major exporter (TB2, Akıncı, TB3) with $1.8bn exports in 2024.
interesting_fact: The Bayraktar TB2 was used so effectively by Ukrainian forces that it inspired a popular folk song. Haluk has received Ukraine's Order of Merit (1st degree, 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He has a BS in industrial engineering from METU (2000) and an MS from Columbia University (2002). During the COVID-19 pandemic, Baykar used its engineering capacity to produce ventilators under his leadership.
notes: Defence/drone company, so pitch carefully. Baykar's press page (https://baykartech.com/en/press/) shows recent space work (Fergani satellites), which could be a podcast angle. The T3 email is the foundation's general contact. Brother Selçuk is the more public figure (CTO, media-facing).

name: Pavan Jain
current_role: Chairman, INOX Group and INOX Air Products (Delhi)
profile: IIT Delhi chemical engineer with 50+ years in industry. He built INOX Air Products from a single plant into India's largest industrial and medical gas maker, and diversified the group into refrigerant gases, cryogenic equipment (INOXCVA / Inox India, listed in 2023) and cinemas (INOX Leisure, merged into PVR INOX). Son Siddharth runs the businesses day to day; his brother Vivek leads the separate Inox GFL group.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he listed cryogenic tank maker Inox India, which debuted at a 44% premium to its IPO price. The same year INOX Leisure merged with PVR to form India's largest multiplex chain.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at IIT Delhi. As chairman of INOX Air Products he grew it from a single plant into one of India's leading industrial gas companies.
notes: Industrial gases and cryogenics (LNG/hydrogen tanks) fit the energy angle. The media-centre email is shown as 'punnet.gupta' in the page text, but the mailto link is puneet.gupta@inoxap.com. Son Siddharth Jain is the more media-active family member.

name: Leonard Abess
current_role: Head of ThinkLab Ventures (Miami real-estate finance and investments); University of Miami trustee
profile: Miami banker (born 1948, Wharton graduate) who became majority owner and chairman of City National Bank of Florida in 1984. The bank his father co-founded in 1946 had about $400m in assets then; he grew it to about $2.75bn and sold his 83% stake to Caja Madrid in 2008 for $927m. He now invests via ThinkLab Ventures, owns about 4,000 acres in Miami and Vermont (some growing limes), and holds a stake in Jersey Jack Pinball.
interesting_fact: He shared $60m of the sale proceeds with 399 current and 72 former employees. President Obama praised him in his February 2009 address to Congress, and Time named him to the 2009 Time 100.
deep_cut_fact: He started at City National Bank in its print shop. With his wife he founded a floating research station in the Brazilian Amazon, and in 2006 he gave $5m to create the University of Miami's Abess Center for Ecosystem Science and Policy.
notes: I found no published contact; thinklabventures.com is a parked domain. Possible routes are the University of Miami Abess Center (he chaired UM's board 2011-2014) or Jersey Jack Pinball. Low media profile since 2009.

name: Ulrike Baro
current_role: Heir and indirect shareholder in Sartorius AG (Göttingen); no known executive role
profile: One of the three daughters of Horst Sartorius, whose roughly 50% stake in lab and biopharma equipment maker Sartorius AG passed to his heirs after his death in 1998. Her great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded the firm in Göttingen in 1870 to make precision analytical balances. Sartorius has about 10,600 employees and revenue above $2.5bn.
interesting_fact: The family stake is held under an executorship that oversees the heirs' inheritance until 2028. She shares the legacy with sisters Karin Herbst-Sartorius and Christine Franken (and Christine's sons).
notes: Extremely private, with no public profile or interviews found; she is a passive heir. The Sartorius media contacts (journalists only) are a corporate route that may not reach her or pass requests on. Low priority.

name: David Penaloza Sandoval
current_role: Founder of Grupo Tribasa / Pinfra (Mexican toll-road operator); no longer on Pinfra's board. His son David Peñaloza Alanís has been chairman since March 2013 and is CEO.
profile: Mexico City construction entrepreneur and UNAM-trained accountant (Forbes gave his age as 79 in 2014). He founded Grupo Tribasa in 1969. After the 1994 peso crisis he renegotiated its debt and brought in new partners, reshaping it into Pinfra (Promotora y Operadora de Infraestructura), which holds toll-road concessions across Mexico. He appeared on the Forbes billionaires list only in 2014.
interesting_fact: He joined the Forbes billionaires list in 2014 after Pinfra's stock rose more than 70% in a year; Pinfra then held 16 toll-road concessions in densely populated parts of Mexico.
deep_cut_fact: He started Grupo Tribasa in 1969 after studying accounting at UNAM. His son, who now runs Pinfra, also trained as an accountant (Universidad Anáhuac) before Harvard business studies.
notes: Probably in his early 90s now, and I couldn't confirm whether he is alive. He isn't on Pinfra's current board (https://www.pinfra.com.mx/consejo-administracion). His son David Peñaloza Alanís is the active figure and a better podcast target for Mexican infrastructure.
